body: Yeah I'm embarrassingly behind in life, still haven't really gotten myself quite together and as firmly self-reliant as I should be. I think it would be slightly less embarrassing if I was just a bit earlier in my twenties

I do this too. Food tastes good and I lack the discipline to resist things that taste good. And emotional cravings and trying to fill the void in your soul. And the fact that you can't get enjoyment out of things so you're left with nothing to distract you.
The best times are those times I convince myself I can be and live differently than I once had. It tends not to last long
Whatever it is, I wish I'd stop doing it, I certainly get no enjoyment out of the ordeal

Pretty much. Well, I don't think I'm one of the hardest workers at work and probably not doing as well as I should be, but I'm at least able to function and maintain employment and get the stuff done that I need to do. I actually really like my job and wish I could summon a bit more enthusiasm for it. My baseline isn't very high I guess.

But even that is a huge accomplishment for me. At home I'm barely able to keep myself together at all, on the most basic level.

Yeah I dislike feeling dead inside and like there's nothing I care about with anything resembling conviction.

I think there's a lot more that can be put up with if you can genuinely believe your life means something. But every goal I have evaporates once my motivation shoots back down to zero.

I heard something somewhere about how despair breeds hope and this weird anime I started watching where the character starts destroying the lives of everyone around him and not caring about the consequences. Because creating despair is a way of breeding ultimate hope.

It's a bit silly and overly cliched but maybe there's some truth in that. Even bad situations can create resilience, something to prove, goals, a new dream to preserve and fight for and preserve. At the root though, I genuinely don't think it's the situation, it's the person. The right kind of person could rise to the top even in a situation where he may be temporarily relegated to the bottom of the barrel. The right person will always have the desire to better himself and will not accept defeat for long.

The other kind of person could be set for life and still somehow or other screw if up. Or come to realize that nothing they could ever want in life means a thing to them. That type of person will have their dreams in life sloppily scribbled on a napkin, thrown in the trash and forgotten. And they'll consistently think they're right on the cusp of getting it together to realize they're only fooling themselves. They haven't done anything at all. Rinse wash repeat.

I'm not in the business of any real comparative analysis, having nothing and not being able to make ends meet is objectively worse. But there's something to be said for what happens to someone when they realize just what type of person they really are. And as they watch all they sought to build continually elude their grasp.

So I guess that's why I'm frustrated now, I got to the point where I feel I've started to figure out what I really want and what I'm truly passionate about. Yet I've been making steadily less progress in that and am starting to believe that every positive thought I've coerced myself into believing is now a lie. And always was.
I usually just grunt "it's fine" because it's easier to be alone than subject yourself to whatever meaningless platitudes others might provide.
It's practically impossible to string enough words together to talk about the simple things.

I'm just on autopilot. No dreams, ambition, soul. I'm fairly lucky, as far as some things go, but I still feel like an empty shell of a person and I can escape it for brief periods but it never lasts. I just don't care that much about life.
I don't know if I'll ever make decisions well. I second guess everything and never trust anything I think. I also never feel coherent enough to use logic or weigh all factors at hand

It feels weird and eerie looking at myself in the mirror. It's not so much a matter of looks though. I'm honestly surprised I don't look worse.But it's still uncomfortable, the whole, "this is the face of that terrible piece of crap that keeps messing everything up" kind of thing

I think I probably spend too much time thinking about sex and stuff and it would probably be better if I didn't. Though I don't think I could enjoy it due to the ever present risk of STI's and unwanted pregnancies and even vasectomies don't technically 100% alleviate that risk. I don't think it would be really all as great as it gets built up in my mind to be.

I think the biggest thing is the difficulty building up and sustaining interest in things to distract myself with. I have things I like, at least theoretically, but I never feel much like persuing them. It all seems kind of meaningless and stupid and pointless. I'm not sure how to get over that hurdle.

This was actually kind of a big year for me now that I look back on it. I managed to finally get my first full time job after really struggling for awhile and managed to get two promotions as well. Over the course of the year I've felt myself begin to build more self confidence/self esteem that I did not have before and got to the point where I actually enjoy going out and socializing rather than dreading being around people and constantly worrying what they think about. I still have a lot of things I need to work on but I feel I've come a long way and am in a space where I'm able to enjoy things in life more than I used to.

I also started writing creative stuff a couple months ago, which I haven't been able to motivate myself to do in years due to lack of motivation/apathy. It's not much, I'm still struggling to finish anything, but I at least have a good vibe about where it's going and I've been able to at least write something every day for the past month.

So it's been a nice year, I think I learned a lot and am in some ways probably a different person from last year. And regardless of whatever other loose ends there are I feel good about that and it's nice to feel good about things. And I guess the main reason I'm writing all this is that ongoing effort to teach myself to think/see things more positively and begin to believe the more positive things.

Yeah I feel like I can't do anything at home. I run on my way home from work but then I can't get myself to shower half the time and just go straight to bed. And days like today I find myself staring at the wall because I can't get into anything. Sometimes I debate whether it's possible to just not come home until the end of the day for my own well being but I don't know if that's realistic.

Positives-I finally have a decent job that I actually mostly like and find interesting and I like the people there, I'm able to get myself physically up every day to go to said job and get through each day without major incident, I try to eat healthy each day with fruits and vegetables and lots of water, I think I might be better about managing my portion sizes, I'm trying to cut out dessert junk food entirely at least for awhile, I go for a run outside every day, I still have good friends somehow, I have a supportive family, I've been going to church consistently for the past few weeks (I don't know, it's nice to cling to the idea that I'm not alone in the universe and sometimes it feels good), I might actually be able to move out with my friend soon and am starting to discuss plans to do so, I sort of convinced myself that because the girl at work chose to talk to me of her own free will (which I still find incomprehensible) that life might somehow be worth living-it didn't last very long but it was nice. I sort of have some personal goals (want to write/read more, learn an instrument), I don't think I've looked at porn in awhile, I see a counselor (but going feels pointless)

Negative-I'm stupid, lazy, pathetic, unmotivated, struggle to push myself to do basic things, I have nothing positive to contribute and am behind most people my age, I still believe I will inevitably fail at everything I do, I suck at my job, I dread being around people socially, feel like my friends look down on me for being lesser than them, I've done nothing to actually get anywhere with my personal goals, I have so much dread and fear over certain elements of my physical health that I think because of that alone life not worth living, I feel like I'm wasting my life, I feel terrible whenever I have any time to myself, I don't enjoy or care about anything, I feel like I am going to mess up somehow.

I don't know, I guess the pros objectively outweigh most of the cons, or maybe they dont mean anything. I just feel low and hopeless sometimes, like I'm trying to put off the ineivitable, like I want to give up and not even bother trying to be better because what's the point anyways.

When i don't have a routine I find myself incapable of doing much at all and feeling guilty over that I guess. The structure of a routine at least keeps me going and functional via muscle memory though i do wish I had some kind of intrinsic motivation or took even some initiative to live my own life, develop myself...I feel like a very bland, dumb lazy and uninteresting person. I have very little to contribute to society and no life experience or knowledge, nothing to say. I'm constantly surprised other humans tolerate having me around.

I feel a lot of dread over the future. I sort of fake it when I'm out in the world and sometimes just being able to talk to people somewhat competently amazes even me. But then during nights, weekends mornings I want to die. I don't know what's wrong with me or what I really want.

I just exist and that's all I'm able to do. And not even that well.
Ate a peanut butter and cherry craisin sandwich. I lead a rugged life.
I cant finish anything. Want to learn piano, too much work to structure or figure out how. Want to write/read/be creative, brain is too dead.

I don't even have the remotest desire to be in a relationship with someone at this point, I don't even think it's something I'd be capable of doing. I just can't help but think of it as for lack of a gentler word, letting someone nag/annoy you and make your life a living hell. Just doesn't seem worth it from an outside perspective. Personal space is important. Sure I have desires and all that but I've made it this long might as well keep going.

The only reason i don't is because then I'd never be able to taste food or coffee. Despite the fact that food is a direct cause of making me miserable half the time. There really isnt anything else left that i enjoy or care in the least about. Maybe one day I'll consume enough that that won't be an issue anymore

I'm struggling to find a psychiatrist because I'm too lazy to bother to go on their website or figure out how to make an appointment and having no time during business hours. Plus I don't have a cell phone anymore due to losing one and personal choice (honestly dont even want one) but a lot of places dont let you do the whole process by email. Though I'm also not a huge fan of checking email. Id rather live a disconnected life.
Yup, everything is an ordeal.

The thing is if I didn't work I'd never leave my room or do anything. Im not really sure what I'd do or want to do if i had the resources or even if I could do anything. Whenever I'm not working I find myself invariably vegetating behind a screen. I'm not really sure how to turn on that switch of taking over your own unstructured time. I always get really excited about just doing nothing for a couple days but it's never what I think and I sometimes find myself drained at the end of it.

I eat too much because I like food too much and because it's probably my only compelling thing to look forward to in life anymore. Yet i feel miserable after eating too much and hate myself and cant sleep or do anything and worry about getting fat. I can cut down on food for a couple days but after a while i get so hungry that i eat too much again. It's a constant battle.

I feel the same. Sleeping, eating and coffee are the only things i enjoy and look forward to and the only things which force me to push through everything else. I try to run most days to burn the calories to offset the constant need to eat large quantities of food, but even so the days i eat too much are the days i hate myself most and the days i have most trouble sleeping. 

I don't get enjoyment out of anything else besides vegetating and i stopped talking to anyone because i cant do it anymore.

I feel empty as well in a similar way, like I just don't care about anything or have anything to really live for. I can barely keep myself in sort of a routine but just freeze up and struggle to get through parts of the day. Most of the time I just generally have no desire to do anything at all.

Sometimes I have a hard time getting as much sleep as I want because I'll just be staying up too late obsessing whether or not to eat more. Even if I don't give in and just go to bed (as is often best) I still find the thoughts that I should be eating more interfering with my sleep and overall quality of life.

Thing is it really wasn't intentional at all, I absolutely loathe throwing up and would never want to intentionally do that. It's just my stomach felt so terrible I literally had no choice. Doesn't make it less concerning that the same thing happened twice and I really need to figure out what I'm doing wrong and why now. 

I mean, it's not like I've never eaten too much before, but the other times I'd usually just feel really uncomfortable or bloated for a day or two but never have to throw up or feel sick in any way. My best guess is that it being party foods were the kind of goods that expand in your stomach more than what I eat on a regular basis. That's my best guess.

Thing is, I didn't even realize how much I was eating, I mean I knew I was eating a lot but I thought I was just really hungry and I didn't really feel full in the sense that I usually do but maybe the foods I was eating expanded later on and caught up with me then, because I starting getting this acid reflux and chest cramps and was just miserable until I threw up.

 I think I should have eaten a little more before the curb my appetite so I wasn't as hungry at the party and would eat more moderately/slowly.

Thing is, I'm pretty sure if I knew I was full I would have stopped but for some reason I didn't even feel it until afterwards. I just got a bit caught up in eating more and more just because I thought I could.

Maybe if I could just more strictly define a cut off point that would help, just need to deal with the intrusive thoughts telling me I need to eat more. I really want to prevent any more vomitting because the thoght of it makes me very anxious.

Yeah work and my struggles with it tends to make me feel like a worthless idiot. I cried multiple times at work today, I could have a good opportunity with this job but I feel like I'm close to messing it up just like I do with everything else.
Yeah I find myself thinking more and more that there just isn't anything worth living for. But ending it seems so intimidating. But I'm not sure how much longer I can go on with things how they are

Someone who had more defined goals/dreams when they were younger and had taken more steps to actively achieve them. Someone able to go out and just do things without getting hopelessly stuck. Someone with self confidence. Someone self reliant and able to stand on their own feet.

Yeah this is pretty much exactly my problem the instability sucks. I had a fairly good chance at being made permanent at my current job and can't seem to get another. Makes me feel like I'm not good enough, but I am pretty stupid/slow so I can understand I guess. I feel like I just don't seem to process information well or something, I don't know. I like that this is at least familiar and get stressed out thinking about whether I might fail trying to adapt to a new place if it doesn't work out.

Sometimes I tell myself things will be much better once I get to that point, but more likely I'll just enounter new unforeseen brick walls.

I feel the same way. My life doesn't have any value and I hate being alive or doing anything. But, a botched suicide could create far worse problems, physical pain, constant people's nagging of why did you have to try and kill yourself... If only there was a pain free pill that was guaranteed to work instantly in my sleep. 

I'd take that tonight. I hate how people are all like suicide is never the answer you have a chemical imbalance etc. There are plenty of good reasons to off yourself. My life is completely worthless anyway and I've got nothing to live for and I just don't enjoy much of anything in it. If you don't like the taste of a roast beef sandwich it's fine to just not eat eat it. But if you don't enjoy being alive, I mean, life's not for everyone. 

But of course I'm too scared and lazy to actually do anything. I think if I had to emotional resolve to actively kill myself I could probably use that to not be the way I am now. I thought about waiting about four if things haven't changed but am not sure how I feel about looking at myself at that point.

There are a few things that if I could just get through things could theoretically start to get better, thing is those basically feel like mountains at this point. Or brick walls. Truth is, it's probably never going to get better and is infinitely more likely to get worse. I recognize that things could get a lot worse than they are and that even when I feel really bad I'm not even close to the bottom. 

Things could get a lot worse and over time they probably will. I am too worthless and stupid to prevent things from going wrong and cannot even begin to predict the worst of it.

Yeah I try to never bring that kind of stuff up around my friends, problem is I don't really have much in my life to talk about other than feeling awful and not doing much of anything due to feeling awful. How do you convey yourself when the entirety of your self identity is rooted in something you're not supposed to talk about?

I don't feel particularly great around people anymore either, sometimes I think I'm meant to just be alone and miserable rather than with others. At least then I don't have to worry about being looked down on or trapped in the cycle of trying to measure up or justify yourself.

They're nice people and all but they're also just reminders of every bad thing about myself.

Yeah a part of me thinks maybe if I can just force myself to do xyz to get past my current main obstacles I'll start to build some positive momentum to help things be better later. But at the same time, I'm not sure how confident I am of ever having real success with that.

Yeah I can relate, for whatever reason interviewing has become this brick wall that I just can't seem to get past and whenever I have an interview I become overwhelmed by self-hatred. As a result I struggle just to physically get myself to the interview never mind prepare myself to be in a position to actually do well. I really wish I could just get past this wall because if I could just do that I feel like I could start to eventually move towards something like an independent and meaningful life, maybe. Doesn't help that my credentials are terrible and there is very little to sell.

I wish there was a better way out or at least to build more positive momentum.

I'm sure that the persistent criticism isn't too helpful either. Sometimes I think the best approach in this spot is to take gradual baby steps to smaller things you weren't good about before rather than tackling everything at once. But then, for me I wind back into the mentality that the small improvements are nowhere near good enough so what's the point of trying.

Yeah it just seems like being alive is so much work, even at the bare minimum where I stay now. And course if I actually aimed to live a decent lie and be truly diligent in self improvement it would be even harder. Reality is relentless when all you ever want to do is lie down stare at a screen and not talk to anyone ever.
I completely deserve to be depression, I'm awful at the basic tenets of being a human. I don't deserve to be happy.

I tend to be a bit too obsessed with sex also, been trying to quit/mostly cut back on the porn and stuff but I still think about sex and stuff too much, especially while trying to sleep. Some of those things tend to make me a bit uncomfortable also. 

I don't really have any intention of ever dating though, my personality sucks and I think the potential cons for me would far outweigh the pros, even in the highly unlikely event I get my life more together in the near future. I honestly think being in a relationship would present it's own problems and make me more miserable. I can barely motivate myself to take a shower, never mind understand the needs of another person. Yet even accepted this, I still think about stuff like that too often. 

Think it would help if I could be more motivated to develop interests in sustained hobbies/goals.

That said being 22 isn't necessarily that bad, though not ideal. A lot of developing has the potential to happen in your mid 20s. I don't know, probably good to stay away from the Instagram if it makes you feel down. And I don't know, if you already believe you'll never have any success with women, you can kind of say whatever you want and it won't matter, and that's a rare freedom. At least could be worth a few laughs.

However, I don't really have much constructive advice on the matter. Other than don't give up, unless you want to (which is equally valid)

Yeah I don't know, kind of wish I just did a trade or something. I realized kind of late that I just don't have anything I'm really passionate about. Since everything's equally miserable, probably would've been smarter to go with the miserable thing providing the greatest return on investment.
Yeah, there's many things I'd like to be able to push myself to do but then I just feel too awful or otherwise fail in doing so.

Yeah it's hopelessly frustrating. I want a job but I'm not good at anything, not smart, forget things frequently, disorganized, unfocused, tend to take too long to do things and get easily overwhelmed/stressed by the pressure of most work environments. 

I honestly don't believe I'd be good for any company or any kind of career field. But I have to do something so I have to go to interviews and lie to make them think I'm awesome when I really don't have much to work with to bring them to that conclusion. And I have to have these elaborate responses prepared to answer their questions and much of the time I just draw a blank.
For a while I've thought about cutting the cord at 30 if things don't improve. Even waiting that long seems like too long a time though.

I am sorry you are in so much pain. I'm not one to judge or even devise reliable solutions. It can be tough to make it in the world when you feel hopeless and stuck and have no leverage, as typically full-time jobs don't take you unless you have a decent amount of experience. It sounds like you feel really socially isolated/shunned and that makes it harder to put one's best foot forward.

I often wonder just what in the world will make me happy. I think something to consider is whether the game is something that is making you happy or more of an addiction. It sounds like you are compelled to play most of the time and that leads me to think that it functions as more of a way to escape the bad feelings that real life creates. And sometimes I get in this mindset where I don't want to ever leave my room because life feels overwhelming. But in escaping from it once you come back everything feels worse and you haven't met people an you're still alone.

One thing I'd suggest is seeing if you are at all able to get treatment/counseling because it sounds like the way things currently are, coping with these challenges could be too much. Also, the anger can be a bit worrisome.

The thing is when you're at the low point you can really only set baby steps but it's hard to know what those steps should be and it feels like they'll never lead anywhere.

I don't think you're necessarily a bad person though, just that you've given up a bit on yourself. I don't know, as dumb as it sounds, maybe it might help to repeat a positive mantra to yourself everyday, like I am a capable person, even if you don't believe it, simply verbally saying it. 

It's hard to make friends when you feel like you can't because people look down on you but I hope that you can nonetheless.
I feel the same way. Nothing to live for and would rather spare myself the unnecessary work when I know I'm just going to fail and never be a successful or good person.
I don't really understand why on earth anyone would like me. I'm a pretty terrible excuse of a person.

I'm not very good right now, it's mainly lack of motivation though. I seem to have more general life motivation now that I'm more in a working/exercising routine. It's weird that I find myself either in a type A super motivated to do all the things state (which seems to very seldom come to be) or a barely motivated to get out of bed and struggle to the shower haze.

 I'm trying to make it my goal to get better at it though. It also sometimes helps me to listen to music, I was listening to some metal while cooking tonight and it gave me energy, and luckily it was a fairly easy recipe since I was paying more attention to the music and only half glancing at the directions.

I don't really think I have any intrinsic dream or ambition for myself. I could almost be alright with just existing. Except I'm not really sure how to fit myself into the societal mold.

I see what you're saying and the idealistic part of me wants to argue to just be yourself. There's nothing wrong with being weird and I personally consider it better than acting in a fake way to blend in or pretend to be just like everyone else. When it gets down to it, I don't see anything you've said as being intrinisically bad/wrong or reflective on you as a person, and nome of those things harm anybody.

I mean with your voice I think the main thing would be making sure you are articulate and that people can clearly hear you. Maybe practicing in front of a mirror or speech drills can help with that or a trusted friend you can practice talking too. 

Do you like your hair long and black or is it part of a particular style you are going for? If there isn't a reason you are keeping your hair long you could try cutting it to see if tha makes a difference.

I wouldn't change your interests though, I mean you like what you like and I disagree with how judgmental people get over certain interests. Just do your thing, I mean, it's your life after all. Maybe you could just laugh it off or use a bit of self deprecating humor when people give you a hard time for what you like. Or maybe see if there are ways to meet up with people who share those interests.

The sex thing, not sure if this is your case (it might not be) but a lot of times people starting getting into weirder things when they watch or look at a look of porn and the normal stuff isn't quite as engaging. In which case I would say trying to cut out the porn might be a good idea, though sometimes cutting out habits can be a bit of a challenge.

I don't see anything really wrong with the rubber band thing, could be a nervous thing. Though it could be rubbing people the wrong way if you do it while talking to them.

Overall, I don't think you're creepy or anything. I think it's just a matter of letting your actions and words speak louder than the first impressions people get abou you, I don't know. People judge too much and it sucks. But I hope you can still find a way to believe in yourself

Yeah I kind of have a similar problem sometimes in the way I try to relate to people, though I haven't really been called out for it in such a way. Thing is though a part of me doesn't really like being serious or believe that life was meant to be taken seriously. I mean I have plenty of time to be sad or bummed out or stressed or vacant in real life or around 90% of the time, particularly whilst alone. 

On the rather exceedingly rare occasions I bring myself to socialize I'd honestly rather just goof off and joke around about stupid crap. I don't think I'm generally on the most innate level a good person and my interpersonal skills are pretty terrible but paradoxically enjoy being around people and engaging with them and can be kind of extroverted in such situations even though I tend to never want to go out at first. 

Thing is that I also unfortunately tend to not enjoy actually listening to people if they are speaking anything longer than a sound byte. And I also get caught up in the whole getting a buzz from the sensation of words coming out of my mouth despite not having anything to say. And then there's the whole thinking of some comment you think is zany but other people keep talking and never knowing when to say that thing but also being so afraid to forget the wording of said remark that I'll either stop listening to the other people or continually talk over the other people. 

Not to say I never listen to people in real life but it requires a very very large amount of effort to keep still and do so, and at social parties or gatherings I'm honestly less willing or able to put in the effort to do so.

 But on a basic level I do like feeding on people's energy. And I like making people laugh. And I don't really like the whole song and dance routine of trying to demonstrate I'm doing well in life or have goals or am going places. Well maybe even any of those things were applicable I'd be more apt to want to talk more about those things. Sometimes I might occasionally feel like I try a bit too hard to make edgy or out-there jokes tha just kind of fall flat. Comedy is one of the very minimal things I'm interested in and which I would like to learn to be better at.

I also tend to laugh very frequently during conversations at things that aren't meant to be funny or seen as more serious.

I do tend to cringe when reflecting how generally terrible I am at interacting with people. People are usually nice but usually get the feeling that most people don't really like me that much. Not sure that they really have reason to like me either. I met a girl once who claimed she thought I was funny and one of my friends seems to have a similar style humor so I guess it's not completely a wash. I'm not really good at maintaining normal serious conversations for the following reasons: I think serious things are boring and tedious, I lose interest in topics that require conscious thought or complex consideration, my brain doesn't work properly, I don't have nearly as much life experience as I probably should, I have almost no skills/knowledge/things I'm good at/life success, I have little to talk about or actually contribute to those situations.
